permanentLimits.note: The two conclusion-function ambiguities the program closed by registered text but never brought to an explicit decision the way R1 and R5.2 were. A1.question: Does an absence conclusion require at least one supporting root, or is complete coverage alone sufficient?
A1.DECISION: DECIDED BY THE OWNER at RUN-20260807-8: complete coverage with an empty evidence ledger yields absent_within_declared_scope. Silence across a fully searched declared scope IS the finding. A decision, not a derivation.
A1.rejectedReading: PRESERVED with its reasoning, per the R1/R5.2 discipline: absence requires >= 1 supporting root, on the argument that an empty ledger is indistinguishable from a search never run -- a receipt asserting bounded absence while containing no evidence at all is the loudest thing the schema can emit (the independent implementer's F7/A1, maintained through all three of its runs). Defensible, and rejected: the search ledger, not the evidence ledger, is the record that the search ran -- coverage is attested per location, and I8/I2/I11/I12 police it; requiring a supporting root would make 'we looked everywhere and found nothing' inexpressible, which is the exact conclusion the protocol exists to bound.
A1.worldsAffectedVerification: confirmed by enumeration at decision time, not trusted: exactly 4 exhaustive worlds (one all-searched location ledger per length 1..4, empty evidence ledger, absence claim), all already concluding absent_within_declared_scope under the registered function (RUN-20260807-8 logs/a1-count-verification.txt)
A1.numericEffect: none -- the registered conclusionFunction text already implements the decided reading and I12 already enforces it; the decision closes the ambiguity without any registration change, like the R5.2 ratification
A1.status: DECIDED (owner, RUN-20260807-8); rejected reading preserved above

A2.question: Does a presence conclusion require complete search coverage?
A2.registeredTextImplies: no: conclusionFunction.presence has no coverage term, so 'supported' is reachable with zero searched locations
A2.alternativeReading: presence also requires search.complete; the affected worlds conclude not_established
A2.consequence: 19,152 of 110,840 receipt-producing worlds (17.3%) change conclusion between the readings -- the largest undecided surface in the kernel. A third implementation reading it the other way would diverge on all of them while passing every invariant (the G5/G4 combination). UNDECIDED: the program records this as an owner decision it did not reach, with both readings preserved. The independent implementer chose the no-coverage reading in IND-1 on the argument that presence is existential; the registered text agrees; neither constitutes a decision of record.
A2.status: owner decision not reached; recorded, not decided
A2.paperEvidence: RUN-20260807-9 traceability audit: the paper's aggregator (section 3) has no coverage input and section 8 imposes coverage on absence claims only -- the registered no-coverage-for-presence reading matches the paper and the alternative reading has no paper basis. Recorded as evidence; the decision remains the owner's and remains open.

correctionRecord.what: The named blocker -- 'KL-000 independent reimplementation' -- was discharged by evidence this record predates, and the record did not know it. The blocker text below is preserved verbatim as superseded, not rewritten.
correctionRecord.evidence: IND-20260807-1/-2/-3 (KL-000/results/independent/): a zero-dependency Rust implementation with hand-written JSON, SHA-256 and PRNG, written from the registered documents, agreeing with the reference on the evaluator's exhaustive partitioning, the complete conclusion function (160/49,480/41,820/19,380 over all 110,840 receipts), and the canonical form and digests for the two pinned receipts C11/C12 (byte-identical, 703 and 691 bytes). Commissioned ONCE, exactly as the superseded text said it should be, serving both KL-000's gate and this kernel's prerequisite. Qualified by LEAK-101 as recorded in KL-000/FINAL-RECORD.md; the qualification travels with any KL-011 use of this artifact too.
correctionRecord.pattern: This is the stale-self-description family again -- a record whose truth expired while the world moved, detected by re-deriving from evidence rather than reading the record. Prior instances: PROV-005 (a deleted remote's cache measured as the remote), ART-101 (a result artifact carrying its predecessor's identity), TEST-101 (a projected verification value inherited unexecuted for three runs), and the DOC-102 miscount chain. The fix is the same every time: records name their evidence, and reviews re-derive rather than re-read. This record now cites what discharged its blocker instead of asserting the blocker.
